sections.name: Foundation & launcher
sections.goal: Run the app on a Windows PC in one click and keep it healthy
sections.includes: Python server, launcher, auto-updates, Health Inspector, bug reports
tips: Start with a one-paragraph spec: 'Windows, local web app, Python stdlib only, one-click launcher, auto-update from GitHub Releases.'
Ask Claude to write a test checklist alongside each feature so fixes don't loop.

sections.name: Look, characters & animation
sections.goal: Make it fun and ADHD-friendly so people come back
sections.includes: Sub-shop scene, Hoagie & Kiwi, Original/Neon themes, music, intro/tour, After Hours, shorts, Alison's avatar and garden shorts, website intro video
tips: Share 2-3 reference images and one sentence of style rules up front ('cel-shaded, thick ink outlines, warm deadpan humor').
Approve a single mockup on a design canvas before any code ('make 3 options, I'll pick one').
Batch visual tweaks into one list instead of one at a time.

sections.name: Money tools
sections.goal: Help people save, invest and see their whole picture
sections.includes: Today's Play, Playbook, Money Plan, My Tab, net worth, Costs, Learn, Give, email digest
tips: Give an example of the exact output you want (a filled-in play card) before asking for the feature.
Ask for 'the smallest version that's useful today' first, then layer on.

sections.name: Betting & fantasy
sections.goal: Honest, organized betting for the full menu
sections.includes: Today's Games price edges, lottery picker, Bet Tracker + charts, Kalshi, Sleeper, After Hours
tips: State the hard rules once in project instructions (no automated sportsbook bets, always show honest odds, 1-800-GAMBLER).
Ask Claude to research which APIs exist before designing screens around them.

sections.name: Integrations & data
sections.goal: Connect accounts and free data so Hoagie sees the real numbers
sections.includes: Alpaca, Coinbase, Kraken, SnapTrade, SimpleFIN, Treasury/BLS/SEC/FRED/Finnhub, integrations catalog
tips: Ask for a ranked shortlist ('top 10 free financial APIs with limits, sorted by usefulness') and pick from it in one message.
Keep one integrations doc as the single source of truth and ask Claude to update it each round.

sections.name: AI brains & agents
sections.goal: Let anyone use the AI they have (or none) and plug in their own agents
sections.includes: Claude/GPT/Gemini/free/no-account picker, fit scores, Agent API, MCP server, webhooks, GitHub autopatcher (Claude Code GitHub Action)
tips: Name the agents you already use (Claude Desktop, n8n, ChatGPT actions) so Claude builds the exact connectors.
Ask for an MCP server early: it lets your own Claude test the app.

sections.name: Hosting, accounts & security
sections.goal: Put it online safely for a small private group
sections.includes: Cloudflare Tunnel website, sign-in, lockouts, tiers (Regular / Zero Cool), sign-in links, key storage, per-person feeds and Sports tab
tips: Never paste passwords or keys in chat: ask Claude for a setup step that prompts you on your PC instead.
Decide the access model (who, what tiers) in the first message about hosting.

sections.name: Demo, tour & docs
sections.goal: Show the whole thing working before anyone connects anything
sections.includes: 10-persona simulated demo, guided tour with Ask Hoagie, README/HTML readme, integrations doc, build logs
tips: Ask for the demo data generator first: every later feature can be tested and screenshotted against it.
Request docs in one format (HTML + short MD) once and reuse the template every release.

sections.name: Cost mitigation: legal entity & service structure
sections.goal: Lower costs and risk by running the project through a business entity and choosing who pays for what
sections.includes: NH LLC as the legal entity, donations vs income, nonprofit option for Learn, user-paid services (SimpleFIN paid by each user, not the host), PC hosting vs paid servers
tips: Ask Claude for a one-page 'decision memo' with options, costs and a CPA question list, then take it to a CPA.
Keep business notes in the owner-only knowledge file so the public app never shows them.

sections.name: Admin & handoff
sections.goal: Give the Zero Cool admins the project story, a download and a way to ask questions
sections.includes: Admin panel, project stats, Ask Claude chat, project zip, CLAUDE.md workflows
tips: Ask for the admin/handoff view at the start so it grows with the project instead of being reconstructed at the end.

overall_tips: Put standing rules in the Claude project instructions (themes, safety rules, code names, 'never paste keys') so they never need repeating.
Send one message per round with a numbered list; Claude plans better with the whole picture than with drip-fed changes.
Ask Claude to keep a running CHANGELOG and build log in the project after every round (it did this here).
Use Claude Code with the GitHub repo connected so changes are committed and released directly instead of zipped.
Ask for screenshots after every UI change; reviewing pictures is faster than reading code.
